title: Bridgework SDK & Gateway Adaptation — Avalon Systems Discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery to map Avalon Systems' gateway/proxy architecture and evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Discussed SDK integration, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, rate limits, quotas, observability hooks, SSO/KMS, and pilot next steps. Customer concerned about VPC-only deployment, audit logs, and ability to route traffic through an internal gateway for consistent auth and observability.
topics: gateway/proxy patterns and sidecar vs edge

Ethan to run sample latency calc and estimated cost for 100TPS baseline (by 2027-06-16)
Avalon to provide traffic profile and example prompt set (by 2027-06-18)
Schedule 60-min technical POC kickoff with Avalon infra team (target week of 2027-06-21)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-11 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Sofia (Redwood) — Lena, Rajiv, Priya, Tomas (Avalon)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): Avalon wants private routing via internal gateway, evaluating dedicated vs hosted; LangChain stack in use; wants observability hooks and token-level cost controls; SOC2/KMS required.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is maya from redwood, im the AE on this account. we have ethan and sofia from the solutions team. how's everyone?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: good, thanks. excited to map this out. we invited our infra and ml leads so we can talk through real constraints.
[00:15] Rajiv Menon: quick note — we're under a VPC-only policy for inference in production, so private deployment is top of mind.
[00:22] Ethan Cho: got it. we'll cover the private options and how the gateway/proxy patterns look with redwood private. also we'll talk SDK flows for langchain/llamaindex.
[00:30] Priya Shah: to add, our current stack uses LangChain in python for orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval augmentation. we also run a custom gateway that does auth and request enrichment.
[00:45] Sofia Nguyen: perfect, that gives us context. quick clarifying q: is that gateway a sidecar per service, or an edge layer?
[00:52] Rajiv Menon: it's an edge layer in k8s — envoy-based — and it proxies internal requests out to various inference endpoints, adds mTLS, and emits traces to our jaeger. we need the redwood integration to fit into that model.

[01:10] Maya Patel: ok, let's do a quick rundown of the options at a high level — hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). hosted is easiest to get started but you lose VPC isolation; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; private drops the control plane into your network so the gateway can talk to it directly.
[01:30] Tomas Rivera: small interjection — security is a must. we need KMS integration for key wrapping, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. does redwood private support HSM/KMS and audit stream?
[01:40] Ethan Cho: yes — redwood private can integrate with customer KMS (we've done AWS KMS and Hashicorp Vault), and audit logs can be forwarded or exported. there's a retention and export config we'll share.
[01:52] Rajiv: are logs pushed, or do we pull them? we prefer push to our SIEM.
[01:55] Ethan: push is supported via syslog/forwarder — we'll send the exact config.

[02:10] Priya: on the SDK side — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex wrappers. how much work to swap endpoints? we have thousands of existing workflows.
[02:20] Sofia: major point — we provide official SDKs (python, node) and adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. adapter usage is basically swapping the llm wrapper and a couple of quick auth bits. often it's a 10–20 line change in code.
[02:33] Priya: that sounds promising, any example repos?
[02:36] Maya: yes, we'll share a repo with examples: langchain_adapter.py, llamaindex_connector.py and a proxy example showing request signing. link: https://redwood.example.com/samples/langchain-adapters (note: placeholder link in transcript)

[02:55] Lena: can you speak to streaming and function calling? we use streaming for certain chat UIs and need deterministic chunking for our clients.
[03:05] Ethan: redwood supports streaming responses and function/tool calling. streaming uses chunked transfer with consistent ordering — sometimes the tokenizer names can be off in transcribes, but from an API perspective you get server-sent-chunks. function calling is model-driven or explicit depending on your payload.

[03:28] Rajiv: rate limits — we have multitenant apps with bursty traffic. how do you handle quotas per token and per route? we need per-team quotas and global fallbacks.
[03:38] Sofia: Redwood has route-level rate limits and token quotas. For Hosted, we enforce at the edge with token buckets; for Dedicated/Private, you can configure rate-limit proxies in your infra or use our built-in policy engine. you can also set canary fallback routes to cheaper models when a quota is hit.
[03:55] Priya: important — fallback can't degrade quality for certain flows, so we need policy-level controls. can we tie rollouts to prompt sets/evals?
[04:04] Ethan: yes, Optimize has model config tied to evals. you can configure which prompts are eligible for fallback and metric thresholds to trigger rollback.

[04:20] [Speaker 2]: uh, sorry, small audio cut —
[04:23] Maya: no worries. moving on to gateway/proxy patterns — common approaches are: sidecar (per pod) where the sidecar handles auth and mTLS to the provider, or an edge proxy that aggregates requests. which fits you?
[04:36] Rajiv: edge proxy. we want one canonical transit path so we can monitor and enrich requests.
[04:42] Sofia: with an edge proxy we usually recommend either the dedicated or private deployment. for private you can put the redwood control plane inside the VPC and route traffic via internal load balancer; for dedicated you can front it with your proxy and route to redwood exposed endpoints with mTLS.

[05:05] Lena: latency is a big concern. what kind of p50/p95 numbers should we expect if we run private in our AWS eu-west-1 region vs hosted redwood? we need p95 under 350ms for short prompts.
[05:18] Ethan: rough numbers: hosted avg p50 ~70–120ms, p95 ~300–400ms depending on region and model size. dedicated with reserved GPU and placement in your region can bring p95 down to ~150–250ms. private (on your infra) has the lowest network overhead if placed in-region — p95 could be under 200ms but depends on your instance types and sequence lengths. we'll run model-specific estimates once you share sample sequences.

[05:50] Priya: about kv cache — we do retrieval augmented generation and long conversations, how is KV cache handled across pods?
[05:58] Ethan: redwood runtime manages KV cache lifecycle and shares or pins caches depending on session affinity. in dedicated setups we can configure cache locality so the same user stays on the same instance for throughput; for hosted it's probabilistic but we offer prefix caching and embedding caches for frequent retrievals.

[06:20] Rajiv: observability — we already run prometheus and jaeger. do you expose metrics and traces?
[06:26] Sofia: yes. we expose Prometheus metrics endpoints (scrape or push gateway) and open tracing-compatible spans. you can add instrumentation hooks in the SDK to emit tracing context. also token-level cost breakdowns are available in the console and via an API.
[06:40] Tomas: can we get a per-request token breakdown in our logs? we need to attribute cost per tenant.
[06:46] Ethan: we can include per-request token metadata in forwarded logs; for private deployments you can write that directly into your SIEM. for hosted we provide a webhook/push events feed you can consume.

[07:05] Priya: latency through our existing edge proxy — we worry about double-TLS and extra hops. any recommended patterns?
[07:12] Sofia: reduce TLS handshakes with mTLS session reuse, keepalive settings, and HTTP/2 multiplexing. also consider a lightweight gateway route that only handles auth and then forwards directly to redwood within the same AZ to reduce hops.

[07:30] Lena: let's get concrete about the pilot. we want to run 10k daily conversations across two products, approx 30TPS peak, with a shift to dedicated if latency is good. pilot success criteria: p95 < 350ms, no data leaving our VPC for production, ability to pull audit logs, and <10% regression in accuracy vs our current on-prem model.

[07:55] Ethan: sounds fine. for pilot we typically do a dedicated evaluation cluster with canary routing and the option to run private if needed. we can enable the LangChain adapters and a small gateway shim to intercept calls for tracing.

[08:10] [00:08:10] Rajiv: question about auth: we use mTLS + JWT claims from our authn system. can we do request signing on top?
[08:18] Maya: yes — redwood SDKs support both bearer tokens and mutual TLS. request signing (HMAC) is supported for edge clients; for private you can rely on your internal mTLS and not expose public keys.

[08:30] Priya: any gotchas with lib versions? our LangChain is pinned to 0.2.11 and LlamaIndex is 1.3.0.
[08:36] Sofia: adapter versions vary — we have compatibility notes. LangChain adapter supports >=0.2.8 but there are subtle breaking changes across minor versions. we'll provide a compatibility matrix.

[08:55] Maya: shifting to cost controls — how granular do you need quotas? per-team, per-route, per-model?
[09:02] Lena: per-team and per-route ideally, and a global daily cap. we also want alerts when cost is trending high.
[09:09] Ethan: ok, we support that via usage policies and alerting. in dedicated you get token-level billing metrics in console; for private we stream metrics to your billing system.

[09:30] [09:30] Rajiv: what about fallback model families? we need deterministic behavior — if primary model is unavailable, fallback to a pinned family with the same temperature settings. can rollbacks be deterministic?
[09:42] Sofia: yes you can pin a set of fallback variants and preserve param mappings so behavior is controlled. the rollout and fallback policies are explicit in the model config.

[10:00] Priya: tia — last technical ask: can we instrument to sample generated tokens and do offline evals for quality monitoring?
[10:07] Ethan: yes — sampling hooks exist in the SDK. for privacy you can hash or redact the payload before exporting. we feed sampled outputs into Optimize where you can run evals and set regression alerts.

[10:25] [10:25] Maya: ok, we'll recap then next steps. i'll share the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private doc and security checklist. ethan will prepare latency/cost estimates for your sample workload; priya will share prompts and traffic profile. we should schedule a POC kickoff with infra to scope networking and a short runbook.
[10:40] Lena: thanks, that works. question — how long is the lead time for private deployment?
[10:45] Ethan: typical private onprem/VPC deployment is 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and certs. Dedicated can be provisioned faster, often 2–3 weeks for reserved pools. Hosted is immediate for dev but not suitable for VPC-only production.
[10:58] Tomas: audit/compliance follow-up: we'll need SOC2 evidence, pen test reports, and architecture diagrams.
[11:05] Maya: we'll attach SOC2 and architecture docs in the follow-up.

Auto-actions (from transcript): shared links and docs references.

End of meeting.
